brief_text: I need to work out whether we push into Germany next year or double down on the UK — that's the decision, and honestly the board is split. We're an 85-person regtech SaaS doing £11.2m ARR, growing about 28% year on year, but UK new-logo growth slowed to 9% over the last two quarters and I think the UK market is maybe 70% penetrated for our segment — that's my gut, not a real number. The goal is to get to £20m ARR by end of FY28 without dropping gross margin below 78%. Germany: TAM is supposedly €400m (that's from the 2025 Gartner regtech sizing, though our head of sales thinks it's inflated, maybe half that once you strip out the banks we can't serve). BaFin licensing will take 9 to 14 months, legal quoted us €250k for the process, and we'd need maybe 6 local hires — say €900k a year fully loaded. We have £3.1m cash and we're profitable-ish, breakeven plus or minus £100k a quarter, so we can't fund a two-year burn on this. Assumption: our UK compliance content localises to the German regime with about 60% reuse — our CTO says it's more like 40%, and if he's right the engineering cost roughly doubles. Two existing customers (both UK banks with Frankfurt operations) have said they'd sponsor a pilot — I have the emails from May. Constraint: we cannot hire more than 8 people total next year, HR freeze from the board, and marketing spend is capped at £1.5m. There's a half-formed idea floating around that we partner with a local player like Regnology instead of going direct — nobody has scoped it, might be nothing. Also worth saying: our NRR is 112%, and if we just focused on expansion we might hit £16m without any new market — Priya's cohort model in the June board pack says £15.8m by FY28 on expansion alone. I honestly don't know whether the Germany window closes if we wait a year — two US competitors raised big rounds in Q2. The CFO wants to wait 12 months, the CRO wants to go now. So: Germany in 2027, or UK depth?

coaching.summary: The decision sits at a genuine fork between growth speed and financial safety, with several key uncertainties — localisation cost, UK saturation depth, and competitive timing — that are currently treated as fixed assumptions rather than ranges. Stress-testing those assumptions before committing will sharpen the board conversation considerably.

bias_signals.detail: The brief states '60% reuse' as the working assumption while simultaneously recording the CTO's contrary view that 'it's more like 40%' and that this 'roughly doubles' engineering cost — treating the higher figure as the planning baseline despite an internal expert disagreement is a classic overconfidence pattern.

The brief acknowledges 'that's my gut, not a real number' about the 70% UK penetration figure, yet this estimate anchors the entire framing of how much headroom the UK depth path has via UK Market Saturation.

The brief frames the choice as 'Germany in 2027, or UK depth?' but also mentions 'a half-formed idea floating around that we partner with a local player like Regnology instead of going direct — nobody has scoped it, might be nothing,' suggesting the partner route is being treated as peripheral rather than as a fully evaluated alternative.

elements_considered_but_excluded: A 'gross margin floor' constraint node was considered but the 78% threshold is already implicitly captured through Cash and Margin Strain flowing to Reach £20m ARR by End of FY28
A 'pilot sponsor revenue' node was considered but the brief does not give enough detail to distinguish it cleanly from Germany New Logo Pipeline

strengthen_items.label: Treat localisation cost as a range, not a point estimate
strengthen_items.detail: The brief records a direct conflict between 60% reuse (your assumption) and 40% reuse (the CTO's view), with the explicit note that 'if he's right the engineering cost roughly doubles' — this disagreement should be surfaced as a formal uncertainty driving Engineering Localisation Overrun rather than left as a footnote.

strengthen_items.label: Formalise the two pilot sponsors as a distinct entry pathway
strengthen_items.detail: The two UK banks with Frankfurt operations who 'have said they'd sponsor a pilot' represent a concrete, lower-capital route into Germany that sits between Enter Germany Directly in 2027 and Partner Entry into Germany via Local Player but is not currently represented as its own option, meaning its effect on Germany New Logo Pipeline and Cash and Margin Strain is invisible in the current structure.

strengthen_items.label: Anchor UK saturation to evidence, not gut feel
strengthen_items.detail: The brief explicitly flags that the '70% penetrated' figure is 'my gut, not a real number,' yet UK Market Saturation flows directly into UK Expansion and Upsell Revenue and ultimately Reach £20m ARR by End of FY28 — validating or bounding this figure would materially change how much weight the UK depth path can carry.

strengthen_items.label: Separate competitive urgency from entry-mode urgency
strengthen_items.detail: The brief conflates 'two US competitors raised big rounds in Q2' with the question of whether to go direct or via a partner, but Germany Competitive Window currently feeds only Germany New Logo Pipeline — it is worth examining whether the window affects the partner route differently from the direct route, since a partner might move faster through BaFin than a solo filing.
